as_told.title: Urartian cuneiform inscriptions misattribute the ruins

plain: The ruins, artifacts and symbols around Lake Van in Turkey are credited by mainstream archaeology to the Urartians, a people of roughly 3,000 years ago, but they built on much older foundations, according to the researcher Matt LaCroix. LaCroix tells Michels, without naming a source, that archaeologists give the Urartians credit because they carved cuneiform, the ancient wedge-shaped writing, into some of the temples. If he is right, a far older and forgotten culture laid the groundwork there.
